confirmed.claim: The expiry section says "No document is assigned for training yet." when documents are assigned but none of their assignees is an active member. On the same tab, the coverage figure and the row say the opposite.
confirmed.evidence: TrainingExpiry.tsx:34 `if (assigned === 0) return 'No document is assigned for training yet.';` is fed from SopRegister.tsx:350 `assigned={trainComp.summary ? trainComp.summary.assigned : null}`. 'No one assigned is an active member' : 'No document is assigned yet' }`, and the row says 'No one assigned to this document is an active member.' (TrainingCoverage.tsx:56).

confirmed.fix: Pass the summary (or noActiveAssignees) to TrainingExpiry and use the coverage KPI's wording: when assigned is 0 and noActiveAssignees is above 0, say that no one assigned is an active member. Add a test for that summary.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. TrainingExpiry.tsx:34 returns 'No document is assigned for training yet.' whenever `assigned === 0`, and SopRegister.tsx:350 passes only `trainComp.summary.assigned`. The server's summarizeQmsTrainingCompliance (training-compliance.ts:113-123) counts only rows whose state is 'assigned', so a document assigned to a job role with no active holders gives assigned 0 and noActiveAssignees 1. In that case readQmsTrainingExpiring returns [] (no active member holds a lapsing receipt), so the line renders. The coverage figure for the same summary goes through data.ts:152 and says 'No one assigned is an active member.' confirmed.claim: A retired document whose signed review date has passed shows the word "Overdue" in its Next review cell. The register's figure line above it says "none overdue for review", and the periodic-review schedule leaves the document out. C1 turned this signal into the explicit word.
confirmed.evidence: SopRegisterRow.tsx:176 `const overdue = isReviewOverdue(d.nextReviewDate);` applies to every status, and :72 renders `Overdue` (C1 changed it from red text and a flag). For a retired row, the server sets next_review_due to `isoDay(row.next_review_date)` (periodic-review.ts:283-286, since in-force-release.ts:25 puts nothing in force once a document is retired). The figure counts from the schedule (SopRegister.tsx:131 `rev.rows ?? deriveReviewDue(docs)`, :231). That schedule excludes retired documents: the server reads `status IN ('effective','in_review','draft')` (mdx-qms.ts:504), and the client derivation keeps only `d.status === 'effective' || d.status === 'in_review'` (data.ts:231).
confirmed.scenario: SOP-010 was retired, and its approval had signed a next review of 2026-10-01. Today the table shows "Retired … 2026-10-01 Overdue". The line above reads "5 controlled documents: …; none overdue for review." and Periodic review says "None is due for review within 120 days." A row and the figure line disagree about the same register.
confirmed.fix: In SopRegisterRow, compute `overdue` only for a document that can be due: `(d.status === 'effective' || d.status === 'in_review' || (d.status === 'draft' && !!d.inForce)) && isReviewOverdue(d.nextReviewDate)`. This is the same rule as the server schedule (mdx-qms.ts:504/513).
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. SopRegisterRow.tsx:176 computes `isReviewOverdue(d.nextReviewDate)` for every status, and :72 renders the 'Overdue' chip. Retirement (document-approval-signature.ts:631-646) leaves next_review_date untouched. in-force-release puts nothing in force for a retired row, so schedule.dueOf (periodic-review.ts:283-286) returns isoDay(row.next_review_date), and adaptDoc (qmsDocumentRecord.ts:27/31) makes that the row's nextReviewDate. The register list (mdx-qms.ts:360-380) includes retired rows under 'All'. The figure line counts from the review-due schedule, which selects only status IN ('effective','in_review','draft') (mdx-qms.ts:504), or from deriveReviewDue, which keeps only effective and in_review (data.ts:231). Neither counts the retired row, so the line says 'none overdue for review' above a row that shows Overdue.

confirmed.claim: While the training-compliance read is still in flight, the expiry section says the assignment count "could not be read". The test asserts this wording for null, so it treats not-yet-read the same as failed.
confirmed.evidence: SopRegister.tsx:350 passes `trainComp.summary ? trainComp.summary.assigned : null`. `summary` is null while useFetchJson is still loading (hooks.ts summaryOf(null)). TrainingExpiry.tsx:33 `if (assigned == null) return 'Whether anyone is assigned to train could not be read, so no all-clear is given.';` renders as soon as the separate expiry read returns [] (:48). TrainingExpiry.test.tsx asserts `render(<TrainingExpiry assigned={null} />)` → /could not be read/.
confirmed.scenario: The SOP tab opens and GET /training/expiring answers [] before GET /training/compliance. The training section shows "Loading training records…". The expiry section under it says (and the polite status region announces) "Whether anyone is assigned to train could not be read, so no all-clear is given." A read in flight is called failed. When compliance then answers, the line changes to the all-clear.
confirmed.fix: Pass the compliance read's state, not only the number: loading, failed or the summary. Say nothing, or the loading line, while it is loading. Keep "could not be read" for a failed read, and make the test cover loading separately.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. useTrainingCompliance's summary is summaryOf(data) (hooks.ts:84-88), and that is null while the first read is in flight, because useFetchJson starts with data null. SopRegister.tsx:350 then passes `assigned={null}`. The expiry read is a separate useFetchJson. When it answers [] first, TrainingExpiry.tsx:48 renders nothingLapsing(null), which is ':33 Whether anyone is assigned to train could not be read, so no all-clear is given.' That calls an in-flight read failed while the training section above shows 'Loading training records…'. TrainingExpiry.test.tsx asserts the 'could not be read' text for `assigned={null}` and has no case for loading, so the test treats loading the same as failed.

confirmed.claim: C2 keeps the register's overdue count derived from the register whenever the review schedule is unread, including when it failed. That derivation leaves out a document whose version in force is under revision. The figure line then says "none overdue for review" over a row marked Overdue.
confirmed.evidence: SopRegister.tsx:131 `const overdueFrom = rev.rows ?? deriveReviewDue(docs);` and :231 `overdueCount = overdueFrom.filter((r) => r.overdue).length`. data.ts:231 filters `(d.status === 'effective' || d.status === 'in_review')`, which drops a 'draft' row with `inForce`. The server schedule keeps it (mdx-qms.ts:513 `row.status !== 'draft' || schedule.inForce.has(...)`). The row's chip still shows it (SopRegisterRow.tsx:176 → :72 "Overdue"), because the row's nextReviewDate is the in-force version's due date (qmsDocumentRecord.ts:27/31).
confirmed.scenario: SOP-001 v1 is in force and its review was due last month; v2 is being drafted. GET review-due returns 500. Periodic review shows its failure. The register line says "1 controlled document: 1 in force, 1 draft; none overdue for review." while SOP-001's row shows "Overdue". The same figure also flashes while the schedule is still loading.
confirmed.fix: Either give no overdue clause while `rev.rows == null` (loading or failed), or make deriveReviewDue keep `d.status === 'draft' && d.inForce` alongside effective and in_review, as the server's rule does. The first also removes the flash while the schedule loads.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. SopRegister.tsx:131 uses deriveReviewDue(docs) whenever rev.rows is null, which covers both loading and failed, and :231 counts overdue rows from it. deriveReviewDue (data.ts:229-234) keeps only effective and in_review. A revised document's row is set to status 'draft' (controlled-document-service.ts UPDATE … status='draft') and carries in_force, and its nextReviewDate is the in-force release's due date (periodic-review.ts dueOf). The server schedule keeps that row (mdx-qms.ts:513), and the row's chip shows Overdue (SopRegisterRow.tsx:176 → :72). The derived count leaves it out, so with a failed or still-loading schedule the line says 'none overdue for review' above an Overdue row. effectiveCount still counts it as in force.

confirmed.claim: The change-log totals line ignores the summary's refusal and offers no way to re-read. A refused summary is said as "could not be read" right above the log's panel, which states the refusal in the classifier's words. The log's Try again re-reads only the log, so a failed totals line stays failed after the log recovers.
confirmed.evidence: ChangeControl.tsx:236 `summary === null ? (sum.error ? 'The change-log totals could not be read.' : …)`. changeHooks.ts returns `failure` from useChangeSummary, but nothing reads `sum.failure` (it is used nowhere in client/src). The panel at :255-262 passes `read={failure}`, and its `retry={onRetry}` is App's `changeReg.refresh` (App.tsx:420), which does not call `sum.refresh`.
confirmed.scenario: A reader whose role cannot see change control opens the tab. The log panel says "Your role cannot do this. Your role cannot do this, so the change log was not read." Above it, the figure line says "The change-log totals could not be read." (a failure, not a refusal) for the same refusal. Separately, after a 500 on both reads, Try again restores the log but the totals line keeps saying "could not be read" until some write happens.
confirmed.fix: Classify the summary failure with readRefusalOf(sum.failure). Show nothing in the figure line while the log panel already reports a failure or refusal. Have the log's retry call sum.refresh too.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. ChangeControl.tsx:236 renders 'The change-log totals could not be read.' whenever summary is null and sum.error is set, for a refusal (403 role, module or scope) as well as a failure. sum.failure is returned by useChangeSummary (changeHooks.ts:122) but nothing reads it, so the C4 headline 'A refused read in Quality is said as a refusal' does not hold for this line. The log panel's Try again is `retry={onRetry}`, which is App's changeReg.refresh. sum.refresh is called only after writes and the editor's back (:193, :218, :245, :530, :553). So after a 500 on both reads, Try again restores the log while the totals line stays 'could not be read' with no way to re-read it.

confirmed.claim: The C5 notice door ('a reviewer's or approver's notice opens the review route at their turn') can never fire in the running app. The notice's document comes from the single-document read, and the server never puts the review route on that read. The test passes only because its mock adds a field the server does not send.
confirmed.evidence: SopRegister.tsx:185 `if(d.status==='in_review'&&myTurn(qmsRouteView(d),meId)){...setRoutePanel(d)...}`, where `d` is `target.document` from `readQmsDocument` (ControlledDocumentTarget.tsx:24, qmsDocuments.ts:57 → `adaptDoc`, so `reviewRoute: r.review_route ?? null`). The server's GET /qms/documents/:id (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:583) returns `ok(res, { ...qmsRegisterRow(rows[0]), ...signatures(document) }, { training })`. Only the list route adds `review_route`, through `withRound` (mdx-qms.ts:377, 399-401). So for an in-review document `qmsRouteView(d)` is `{kind:'legacy'}` (qmsReviewRoute.ts:40), and `myTurn` returns null for anything that is not 'live' (qmsReviewRoute.ts:48). The test qmsReviewRoute.test.tsx:254-256 mocks `GET /api/mdx/qms/documents/21` with `review_route: ROUTED`.
confirmed.scenario: Rae is the named reviewer whose step is open on SOP-021, which is bound and under review on a live route. She opens her notice, which carries params {qmsDocumentId:'21'} (notification-record-target.ts:109). The single read has no review_route, so the branch is skipped and line 186 runs `setEditingId(d.id)`. She lands in the editor, which cannot sign: the exact defect C5 says it fixed. The README's 'Walked in the running app' covered only the legacy Open, not this door.
confirmed.fix: Decide the turn from the register row, which carries the route: `const row = docs.find(x => x.id === d.id); if (row?.status === 'in_review' && myTurn(qmsRouteView(row), meId)) {...}`. Wait for the register read and add `docs` to the effect's deps. Alternatively, have GET /qms/documents/:id attach `withRound`. Then make the test's single-read mock match the real response shape, with no review_route.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed by tracing the code. The notice's document comes from readQmsDocument (qmsDocuments.ts:52-56), which goes through adaptDoc and sets `reviewRoute: r.review_route ?? null` (qmsDocumentRecord.ts:34). GET /qms/documents/:id (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:566-583) returns `{ ...qmsRegisterRow(rows[0]), ...signatures(document) }`. qmsRegisterRow (mdx-qms.ts:334-337) only removes metadata.authoringContent and adds no round. qms_documents has no review_route column (only migrations/20261023_review_routes.sql defines routes). Only the list route attaches the round, through withRound (mdx-qms.ts:380, 399-401). So for an in-review document, qmsRouteView(d) returns {kind:'legacy'} (qmsReviewRoute.ts:40) and myTurn returns null (qmsReviewRoute.ts:48). SopRegister.tsx:185 is skipped and line 186 opens the editor. The effect's deps (line 188) do not include the register, so it never re-runs once `docs` arrives with the route. The notice reaches this door from TaskBoard.tsx:1610 (params {qmsDocumentId}) and notification-record-target.ts:109. The only test is qmsReviewRoute.test.tsx:254-256, and its single-read mock adds `review_route: ROUTED`, which the real server never sends. The test passes for the wrong reason.

confirmed.claim: For a legacy entry past draft, the new "Open" leads to the same personal training reader the commit says it replaced: an overlay titled "Read and acknowledge", with its own "Edit controlled text". The commit and README say it opens the inline text "read-only", and the row header says Open opens the one editor on every row.
confirmed.evidence: SopRegister.tsx:195-199: `if (d.authoringDocumentId) setEditingId(d.id); else if (d.status === 'draft') setSetup(...); else openReader(d.id);`. openReader mounts PersonalTrainingReader (SopRegister.tsx:366-367), whose title is 'Read and acknowledge' (PersonalTrainingReader.tsx:71) and which shows 'Edit controlled text' when `mayEdit` holds (PersonalTrainingReader.tsx:39-42, 87). The server sets canEditControlledText for any governed-write member on an unbound draft or in_review document (server/services/qms/training.ts:118-119). The commit's own screenshot (docs/evidence/DESIGN/D7/2026-11-10-open-door/shots/w7-open-legacy-text.png) shows 'Read and acknowledge' and an 'Edit controlled text' button. The commit message, the README table and the comment at SopRegister.tsx:191-194 say 'read-only'. SopRegisterRow.tsx:13-16 says 'Open' opens 'the one editor, on every row', replacing an overlay 'titled "Read and acknowledge" with an edit path of its own'.
confirmed.scenario: The author opens QS-SOP-001, a legacy entry under review, with Open (the README's own walk). They get the Read-and-acknowledge overlay with 'Edit controlled text'. That edits the controlled text of a document under review outside the editor. A legacy effective Form, whose next step is now 'Open', lands on an overlay titled 'Read and acknowledge' that says 'This document type is not controlled read-and-understood training.' (training-content.ts:62): the confusion C5 says it removed. The walk script w7-open.cjs is headed 'reaches the one editor' but logs `editing:false, reader:true, back:false` and records ok:true.
confirmed.fix: Either open legacy past-draft text in a truly read-only view titled for what it is, by giving the reader a read-only mode with no 'Edit controlled text' and a neutral title, or correct the commit, README, code comment and SopRegisterRow header to say Open reaches the training reader, with its edit path, for legacy entries.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. openDocument (SopRegister.tsx:195-199) sends a legacy entry past draft to openReader, which mounts PersonalTrainingReader (SopRegister.tsx:366-367). That overlay is titled 'Read and acknowledge' (PersonalTrainingReader.tsx:76) and offers 'Edit controlled text' (line 87) whenever mayEdit holds (lines 38-42). The server sets canEditControlledText for a governed-write member on an unbound draft or in_review document (server/services/qms/training.ts:118-119), so a legacy entry under review is editable from Open. The code comment at SopRegister.tsx:193, the commit message and the README row (open-door/README.md:15) all say 'read-only'. SopRegisterRow.tsx:13-16 says Open opens 'the one editor, on every row' and implies the reader overlay with its own edit path is gone. A legacy effective Form's next step is 'open' (SopRegisterRow.tsx:115), which lands on the 'Read and acknowledge' overlay. The README's 'Not done here' admits the title and the second edit path, but its claims of 'read-only' and 'the one editor on every row' remain false.

confirmed.claim: The periodic-review row's door moved from the training reader to the editor. The editor read is refused (403) to assigned trainees who have no authoring grant, and that refusal is shown as 'could not be opened' with a Try again that can never succeed. The reader admitted them.
confirmed.evidence: Before 1a69d42a1: `onOpen={openReader}`. Now: `onOpen={(id) => { const d = docs.find(...); if (d) openDocument(d); }}`, so a bound document goes to `setEditingId`. The editor read GET /qms/documents/:id/editor requires authoring 'view' (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:453-454 → 403 QMS_DOCUMENT_VIEW_DENIED). 'view' needs a doc_permissions grant or global admin (server/services/authoring/authoring-permissions.ts:231-253). The reader's read admits an assignee without that grant (server/services/qms/training-assignment.ts:390-394: an assignee skips authorizeQmsContentRead). ControlledDocumentWorkbench.tsx:42 renders `<ErrorState title="The controlled document could not be opened" message={error} retry={() => void load()} />` with no `read=`, so the refusal keeps a retry.
confirmed.scenario: An operator is assigned by job role to train on SOP-015 (bound, effective, due within 120 days) and has no doc_permissions row on its authored copy. Before C5, 'Open SOP-015 … for its periodic review' opened the reader with the version in force. Now it opens the editor: 'The controlled document could not be opened — You do not have permission to view this authored document.' and a Try again that always gets the same 403. The commit itself calls this pattern a dead end for the legacy case.
confirmed.fix: Keep a door that this reader can pass. Either open the reader (or a read-only view) for a document the person cannot view in the editor, or classify the editor read's 403 in ControlledDocumentWorkbench: carry status and code through readQmsEditingCopy and pass `read=`, so the refusal is said without a retry, and offer the reader as the way to read it.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. Before 1a69d42a1 the periodic-review row passed `onOpen={openReader}`. It now calls openDocument, so a bound document goes to setEditingId and ControlledDocumentWorkbench. GET /qms/documents/:id/editor (mdx-qms.ts:445-456) requires authoring 'view', and 'view' needs a doc_permissions row or global admin (authoring-permissions.ts:231-261). Otherwise the route returns a 403 with QMS_DOCUMENT_VIEW_DENIED. authorizeQmsTrainingRead (training-assignment.ts:390-394) admits an assignee to the reader only, and its own doc comment says 'not the editor'. review-due (mdx-qms.ts:498) is open to every org member, so a trainee sees the row. ControlledDocumentWorkbench.tsx:42 shows any error with `retry={() => void load()}`. readQmsEditingCopy throws a plain Error with no status, so the 403 is a retry that can never succeed.

confirmed.claim: Each periodic-review row's Open is now disabled whenever the register read is unread or failed, even though the review schedule (its own read) listed the row. No reason is given.
confirmed.evidence: 1a69d42a1 changed `canOpen={canOpen}` (personalTrainingScope: independent of the register) to `canOpen={(id) => docs.some((x) => x.id === id)}`. `docs` is `reg.docs ?? NO_DOCS` (SopRegister.tsx:126), so it is empty while the register is loading or failed. PeriodicReview.tsx:119 `disabled={!canOpen}`, and the only title is 'Open the controlled document' (line 118).
confirmed.scenario: The register read returns a 500 while GET /documents/review-due answers. The panel lists 'SOP-015 Supplier controls · Overdue', but its Open button is disabled with no explanation. Before C5 the same button opened the document's text.
confirmed.fix: Keep the door usable without the register: `canOpen={(id) => docs.some((x) => x.id === id) || (regUnread && canOpen(id))}` and `onOpen={(id) => { const d = docs.find((x) => x.id === id); if (d) openDocument(d); else openReader(id); }}`. The other option is to give the disabled button a title that says it waits for the register.
confirmed.verifier: Confirmed. In SopRegister.tsx:344, canOpen is now `docs.some(x => x.id === id)`, and `docs` is `reg.docs ?? NO_DOCS` (line 126). PeriodicReview.tsx:119 sets `disabled={!canOpen}` with only the title 'Open the controlled document' (line 118). The schedule read is independent of the register (hooks.ts:44-65), so a failed or in-flight register read with a resolved schedule lists rows whose Open is disabled with no reason. Before the change, canOpen was personalTrainingScope, which does not depend on the register. The register's own ErrorState appears above, but nothing ties the disabled button to it. Low severity.

refuted.claim: C4 sends Quality's per-record reads through the refusal classifier without a subject. A 404 on a controlled document or a CAPA is therefore said as "This project was not found in your organization". Quality's records belong to the organization, and the thing missing is a document or a CAPA, not a project.
refuted.reason: Not reachable as described. The wording path is real: readRefusalWords (dataConnect.tsx:569-571) calls describeReadFailure with no subject, and that defaults to 'this project'. But the 404s the finding relies on have no user-reachable trigger. (1) TrainingAssignmentsPanel opens only from a row of this organization's register (SopRegister keys its session by org and user). readTrainingDocument returns null only for a document outside the organization or one with deleted_at set, and nothing in server/ sets deleted_at on qms_documents: no DELETE route and no soft-delete UPDATE. The scenario's 'another user deleted the document' cannot happen. (2) capa_records also have no delete path. The CAPA detail 404 a user can actually meet comes from authorizeCapaProgram (governed-context.ts:121, 'Project not found.'), because CAPAs belong to a program/project, and for that 404 'This project was not found in your organization' is accurate. No user-visible false statement is shown.

refuted.claim: C4 adds the library failure panel inside the Controlled documents section with no regard for the register's own failure. One refusal of the Quality routes is therefore said twice in the same section, as two assertive alerts.
refuted.reason: Not a defect. Both panels are true statements about two distinct reads: 'the controlled-document register was not read' and 'the Quality system library was not read'. Each has its own retry for a failure. That is the per-read rule C4 applies across the whole tab: PeriodicReviewPanel, TrainingCoverage and TrainingExpiry each also state the same refusal for their own read, so a guard on the library panel alone would not make one cause 'said once' anyway. The 'said once (C4)' comment refers to why 'New controlled document' waits. It is not a claim that causes are deduplicated across reads. Two role=alert regions for two failed reads is not a misused role or a lost focus. Nothing false is said and no accessibility rule is broken, so this is a presentation preference.
